people.paul.role: Writer who corrects the Thessalonians and asks for prayer
people.paul.relations: He writes with Silvanus and Timothy. He calls the readers brothers.
people.paul.meaning: Paul thanks the Thessalonians for growing faith in suffering. He asks them not to be shaken by a letter said to come from him. He tells them to withdraw from brothers who will not work. He signs the greeting with his own hand as the sign in every letter.
people.silas.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Timothy
people.silas.relations: The letter names him first after Paul. Timothy follows him.
people.silas.meaning: The letter names Silvanus in the opening line with Paul and Timothy. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
people.timothy.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Silvanus
people.timothy.relations: The letter names him last, after Paul and Silvanus.
people.timothy.meaning: The letter names Timothy in the opening line with Paul and Silvanus. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
people.jesus.role: Lord who will come, bring relief, and judge
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls him the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul links the readers’ calling and comfort with him.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says the Lord Jesus will be revealed from heaven. He will give relief to the afflicted and punish those who do not obey. Some claim the day of Christ has already come. Paul answers that it has not, and he gives no date.
places.thessalonica.summary: The letter is addressed to the assembly of the Thessalonians in chapter 1. Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy greet them.
places.thessalonica.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: All three chapters are the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: The letter names Paul as its writer. The guide did not check authorship, dates, manuscripts, or Greek forms. It did not check who the lawless one is or what restrains him. It did not check why some refused work. The guide names no present person or event as part of the predicted sequence.
sources.wyant-thessalonians.summary: Wyant reads the work commands as an answer to irresponsible conduct in the group.
sources.wyant-thessalonians.limits: This is Wyant’s own reading. Her ideas about who the busybodies were are only options. The guide did not check her Greek analysis, military usage, or the Didache. It did not check the linked news report.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-43.summary: The lesson studies work and a falling away before Christ’s return.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-43.limits: Second Thessalonians coverage follows what the lesson discusses in chapters two and three. Its link to the Great Apostasy is Church teaching. It is not independent historical evidence. The guide did not check the linked Restoration passages.
sources.net-thessalonica.summary: The dictionary places the city on the Thermaic Gulf and gives coordinates.
sources.net-thessalonica.limits: Only the opening place description and the coordinates support the marker. The guide did not check old population figures, wider history, inscriptions, buildings, or routes.
chapters.*.mapNote: The map marks Thessalonica as one city point. The map has no point for the temple of God.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The letter gives no delivery route.
